scope: Independent read-only review of Phase A metadata observation/strict extraction, Phase B owner recovery policy, original 20 boundary cases, two added same-owner registry cases, and the proposed mounted-App import/close fixture. Existing recorded results were inspected; this reviewer ran no tests, browser, typecheck or native commands.

invariants.assessment: Each read, write, single CAS and multi-key CAS registers its settle-only barrier before invoking its body. A first CAS is visible before a memory generation exists. Multi-key observations cover written keys. Existing storage values, owner/generation checks, atomic commit and journalFlush persistence ownership remain authoritative.

All three exact owner keys must have settled failed reads, no successful read, acquired record or local work, followed by a successful ordinary journalFlush. Successful empty recovery, source actions, writes, CAS attempts, staged records, broadcast and enumeration acquisition remove the allowance. Foreign owner metadata still rejects.

A false CAS, ordinary read, automatic accepted-source cleanup, or older successful operation cannot retire a newer source failure. Explicit committed source edit/import retries acknowledge earlier operations only for their written keys. An exact persisted ordinary generation retains journalFlush retry ownership.

journalRecoveryOperation installs a global renderer recovery barrier before file parsing/reference lookup. Source handoff settles it before inspecting source failures; its revision forces another inspection if import begins during an await. DraftTransfer uses the wrapper on the actual action and a settle-only registry guard for ownerless transfers. No registry recursion.

Metadata obligations remain keyed to full thread/project/workspace identity across A to B to A. Existing render epoch/current-owner and abort checks remain. Attach and refresh mark current source editing work; source Open remains readonly.

Only metadata and settling promises are added. The original journal remains the draft/source value owner. No new host grant, request authority, duplicate composer or persisted ownership record is introduced.

investigatedFindings.origin: An earlier unsealed transfer guard could settle after a failed imported CAS while a concurrent source guard had already approved before that CAS.
investigatedFindings.resolution: The global metadata barrier is registered before preprocessing and source handoff drains/rechecks it. Real registry/import/CAS fixtures cover held preprocessing success and failure. The failure case is red under Phase A and green under Phase B.
investigatedFindings.limit: Focused tests invoke the actual wrapper but do not mount DraftTransfer; the separate browser fixture is not yet executed at review.

investigatedFindings.origin: Concurrent App/provider helper reads contribute pending/revision observations, raising a possible repeated-read concern.
investigatedFindings.evidence: Both appended tests passed on unchanged Phase B: retained same-owner source/text, and held pending hydration while a new source generation commits. Each delegates real journalHandoffState snapshots and has a 64-inspection non-progress sentinel.
investigatedFindings.conclusion: No observed loop or actionable production defect established. No coalescing or timeout change was made or is justified by these results. The bounded fixtures do not prove every scheduling pattern.

browserFixture.assessment: No material static fixture defect found. Actual File.text is held before component parsing; actual journal barrier is read; actual DesktopProvider close callback enters the shared registry. Source-key IDB put failure aborts the bundle. The test requires false close, retained input DOM, no committed text/source, another blocked close, then exact explicit import retry and true close. Task/split and native bridge remain scripted.
browserFixture.sourceVerification: Proposed file equals preserved base bytes plus the new addition. Existing tests and deadlines are unchanged.
browserFixture.authorityLimit: Source identities in this backup are inert fixture records. No real host source grant, installed desktop or native platform claim.

limitations: Phase A is deliberately strict: 11 passed and 12 failed across two actual files. Its failed receipt remains retained, not reclassified as a baseline pass.
Phase B has 25 passed, zero failed and zero skipped across two actual files: 22 source cases and three existing registry cases. JSON suite totals include nested describes and are not file counts.

Focused IndexedDB, localStorage and BroadcastChannel are scripted. Actual journal, recovery, parsing, generations, CAS, import and registry execute. This is not real browser storage, installed desktop or Windows proof.
The A to B to A case checks metadata persistence and the owner-fence helper, not a full React/native-window lifecycle.
Source action marking excludes the cold allowance; it does not add a new barrier around the entire host capture/refresh request when storage is healthy.
Mounted DraftTransfer browser validation, broader regression, and exact-head target execution remain separate gates.
reviewerMutations: Only this outside-repository review directory was written. No repository/index/ref/remote mutations or test execution.
